correctness.rationale: For any specified set of k disjoint adjacent cyclic chords, probability of inclusion is (2n-2k-1)!!/(2n-1)!! and conditioned residual crossing count has law X_{n-k}. There are M_{n,k} such boundary matchings, whence E[binom(S,k)f(X)]=M/prod E f(X_{n-k}). Expanding u^S proves the finite joint PGF. First two factorial moments yield E S=2n/(2n-1), Var S=4n(n-1)/(2n-1)^2, Cov(X,S)=-2n(n-1)/(3(2n-1)); combined with Var X=n(n-1)(n+3)/45 yields negative correlation -sqrt(5/(n+3)). Uniform factorial bounds and crossing CLT establish the independent Gaussian–Poisson joint limit. Independent exact complete matching counts n=2..7 check each k and crossing coefficient.
residual_risks: n=1 is excluded from cyclic simple-chord definitions; the finite negative correlation is not finite independence.
